title: Maschinentechnische Ausrüstung Gasspeicher & Gasfackel
description: Die Speicherung des in der Faulung produzierten Gases erfordert den Neubau eines Gasspeichers als gewichtsbelasteter Niederdruckgasspeicher. Der Bestands-Gasspeicher wird nach Neubau und Inbetriebnahme der Neuanlage des gewichtsbelasteten Niederdruckgasspeichers zurückgebaut. Für den Gasspeicher wird eine Fundamentplatte aus Stahlbeton hergestellt. Das anfallende Kondensat wird dem Kondensatschacht im freien Gefälle zugeführt. Der Boden des Stahlgasspeichers nimmt das Gefälle der Sohle auf. Der Behälter besteht aus einem zylindrischen Gehäuse aus Stahlblech, einem konischen Dach, einer beweglichen Scheibe und einer rollengelagerten Teleskopführung. Die Membrane ist als Kegelstumpfmantel konfektioniert. Zur Ausbildung des veränderlichen Gasraumes dient eine ausgesteifte Scheibe, der nach Bedarf Belastungsmaterial zur Erzeugung des Gasdruckes aufgelegt werden kann. Es kann ein max. Betriebsdruck von 55 mbar erfolgen.

title: IN-ORBIT RECONFIGURABLE SOLAR ARRAY - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To design a solar array concept allowing for in-orbit reconfiguration of strings length and section size and to optimisethe solar array power output for EOL best possible performance.Description: Solar cell voltage and current are a function of operating temperature and degradation level. String lengths and section sizes are optimised for EOL best performance. However, this means that for most of the time the solar array is not exploiting its full performance capability. If string lengths and section sizes were reconfigurable, the power output at each time of the mission could be maximised. This concept could provide various benefits, such as flexible adaptation in case of unforeseen events (e.g. solar flares, micrometeorite impacts, etc.), mission extension in GEO and potential use of cells with less performance in GEO radiation environment. These benefits can be of interest for Telecom applications, where very large solar arrays are typically required to compensate for the degradation over the entire mission. This activity targets innovative photovoltaic assembly concepts that allows for reconfiguring string lengths and section size to optimise performance in dependence of operating conditions during the mission (e.g. temperature, irradiation level). This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Definition of a solar array / photovoltaic assembly concept allowing for reconfiguration of string lengths and section sizes. - Prototyping of interconnection concepts. - Initial proof of concept demonstration.

title: DEVELOPMENT OF AN ELECTRIC THRUSTER OPTIMISED FOR SATURN TRANSFER FOR THE L4 SPACECRAFT (C219-0016MP)
description: The European Space Agency's next Science large-class mission (L4) will be dedicated to exploring Saturn's moon, Enceladus. Known for its active plumes and subsurface liquid ocean, Enceladus is a prime candidate in the search for extraterrestrial life. The missionis set to launch in 2042, with the spacecraft being assembled in space before embarking on its journey to Saturn. The spacecraft will sample Enceladus' plumes in 2053 and land on its south pole in 2058. Solar electric propulsion is the main candidate for propelling the spacecraft.The goal of this activity is to develop an electric thruster for the L4 spacecraft as propellant. The thruster shall be able to provide a specific impulse of at least 2500 s over a large power range [i.e. 9 to 20 kW] and a total impulse capability of at least 4 MNs/kW. As part of this activity, also a preliminary assessment of a dedicated test facility, to support development and qualification of such thruster, of shall be performed.
